headline: South Asia: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence.
- Persian Gulf Region: Russian strikes kill eight, injure dozens across Ukraine.
- Western Russia: Ukrainians' biggest concerns are corruption and Russian missile and drone attacks – poll.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: POWERING UP AGAIN - Western schools looking towards solar installations post-Melissa.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: POWERING UP AGAIN - Western schools looking towards solar installations post-Melissa.
WESTERN BUREAU: At least two western Jamaica high schools that were damaged during Hurricane Melissa last October are looking to expand the solar-power facilities they had prior to the category-5 hurricane as a means of providing long-term renewable energy to power their operations. Muschett High School in Wakefield, Trelawny, and Herbert Morrison Technical High in Montego Bay, St James, were among hundreds schools pounded by the hurricane on October 28 last year. It wrecked the small solar-power infrastructure they had in place at the time.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukrainians' biggest concerns are corruption and Russian missile and drone attacks – poll.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Ukrainians' biggest concerns are corruption and Russian missile and drone attacks – poll.
A KIIS poll shows that 50% of Ukrainians are concerned about corruption and 40% about Russian missile and drone attacks, while 72% believe corruption has increased since the full-scale invasion.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: US ambassador to NATO believes Ukrainian deep strikes inside Russia bring peace talks closer.
US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker stated that Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian territory help push Moscow and Kyiv towards diplomatic talks.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Three people killed, including Azerbaijani national, and eight injured in Russian attacks on Kyiv Oblast.
Three people were killed and eight others injured in Russian attacks on Kyiv Oblast on 27 September. Civilian facilities, including warehouses, homes, businesses and vehicles, were damaged.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russia attacks business centre in Dnipro: four people injured, some evacuated, some being searched for – videos.
Oleksandr Hanzha, Head of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration, has reported a Russian strike on central Dnipro that caused a fire and left people injured. Four people are known to have been injured so far, and search and rescue operations are ongoing.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Hostile Reactions to Kosovo Wartime Leaders’ Verdict Miss Key Point: the Victims’ Ordeal.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: Hostile Reactions to Kosovo Wartime Leaders’ Verdict Miss Key Point: the Victims’ Ordeal.
Predictable criticisms of the Hague verdict convicting four Kosovo Liberation Army leaders of war crimes ignore the question at the trial’s heart – who the victims were, and what compensation they deserve.
- Politico Europe, just now: EU seeks NATO-style response to Russian hybrid attacks.
The bloc's defense ministers will consider an emergency security protocol amid Moscow's growing threats across Europe.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence.
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Minister slams KP govt’s ‘flaws’ in leadership, resources and authority in counter-terror fight.
Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry on Monday said the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government had not made adequate efforts to combat terrorism, particularly highlighting flaws in its leadership, resources and use of authority. Addressing media in Islamabad alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Chaudhry noted that a political leadership could “provide three things in the fight against terrorism: leadership, resources and powers”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: CM Afridi wants KP input included in counterterror policy.
KP CM Sohail Afridi and his predecessor, Ali Amin Gandapur, inquire after those injured in the Darazinda attack.—Dawn DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday called for better cooperation between the provincial and federal governments on security matters, saying the counterterrorism policy should reflect ground realities. The chief minister made these comments during his visit to Dera Ismail Khan to visit the wounded, a day after a deadly bombing targeting a police and customs check-post killed more than 12 people, including rescue officials, in Darazinda.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: UK police question five men held at airbase used by US to attack Iran.
British police were questioning five men on Monday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after they were detained near an airbase that has been used by the US to strike Iran. Officers detained the three men in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England. US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do “big damage” and had been under investigation by British and US authorities.

- Times of India - Top Stories, The Moscow Times, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Russia strikes Ukraine's largest mobile service provider.
The recent Russian assault on Kyivstar's headquarters has inflicted significant damage to Ukraine's top mobile service provider. With communications infrastructure under constant threat, both military and civilian communications are gravely impacted. The strikes disrupted several data centers, leaving thousands without internet access. Reliable digital connectivity is paramount for Ukraine's military operations, and the disruption poses serious risks during this ongoing conflict.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Archaeologists saved 30,000 treasures from ISIS during Syria war: Study.
In a remarkable feat illustrating tenacity and dedication, Syrian archaeologists embarked on a dangerous mission in 2014-2015 to salvage around 30,000 artifacts from the Deir ez-Zor Museum amidst the intense conflict with ISIS. Led by Professor Maamoun Abdulkarim, the operation faced significant challenges yet underscored the urgency of preserving Syria's cultural heritage and collective memory, reinforcing the crucial role historical artifacts play during times of crisis.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: After hydrogen, India gets its first LNG train; check details.
The dual-fuel arrangement allows LNG to substitute for around 40 per cent of diesel consumption. The move is part of the national transporter’s broader push to reduce carbon emissions and move towards more sustainable modes of transport. A full tank of LNG is expected to support around 1,600 km of operations, thereby reducing the frequency with which the train needs to refuel.
